# 3B.1 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Scholz’s government used torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, extrajudicial killing, or arbitrary punishment against residents. The strongest positive evidence is indirect: he repeatedly backed civilian protection, humanitarian law, ceasefires, and restraint on military force, especially regarding Gaza and Ukraine. Because Germany was not waging a domestic counterinsurgency or repression campaign in 2024, the record is mostly about **preventing or limiting harm abroad**, not about direct protection from state violence at home.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Joint Statement on Gaza** | Federal Government | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/joint-statement-from-the-leaders-of-the-united-states-argentina-austria-brazil-bulgaria-canada-colombia-denmark-france-germany-poland-portugal-romania-serbia-spain-thailand-and-the-united-kingdom-on-gaza-2290942 | Scholz joined a statement calling for an immediate ceasefire, unconditional hostage release, protection of civilians, large-scale humanitarian aid, and compliance with international humanitarian law. It also opposed annexation and backed a negotiated two-state outcome. This is the clearest direct evidence that his policy posture favored civilian protection over abusive force. | 3B.1, 2B.4, 2B.7, 2B.10 |
| **The Latest | Fighting escalates in Rafah as Israel pushes ahead with its offensive** | AP | 28 May 2024 | https://apnews.com/article/20df7de040cec3396a2febe481e4fe72 | Scholz said the Rafah strike that killed civilians showed why Germany and others opposed a large-scale offensive there. He said an Israeli investigation was “right as it is necessary” and tied his position to international law and unacceptable civilian harm. This is strong evidence of support for civilian protection and lawful review after harm. | 3B.1, 2B.9, 2B.4, 2B.5 |
| **Interview des Bundeskanzlers mit der taz** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/aktuelles/scholz-interview-in-der-taz-2270696 | Scholz said he had warned against a Rafah ground offensive, insisted that more humanitarian aid had to reach Gaza, and said every arms delivery was carefully assessed in advance. This is evidence of restraint and precaution rather than indifference to civilian harm. | 3B.1, 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.7 |
| **Summer press conference with Federal Chancellor Scholz** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said Israel has the right to defend itself, but warfare must comply with international humanitarian law and humanitarian aid must reach Gaza on a large scale. He also reiterated support for a two-state solution. This is explicit civilian-protection and lawful-conduct language. | 3B.1, 2B.4, 2B.10 |
| **Bundeskanzler Scholz zum Ende der UN-Mission in Mali** | Bundesregierung | 13 Apr 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/newsletter-und-abos/bulletin/scholz-ende-un-mali-2271088 | Scholz said the Bundeswehr’s Mali deployment was right and that the mission’s original goals were justified. This is not a strong accountability statement, but it is relevant because it does not indicate acceptance of abusive conduct; it reads as a defense of a peacekeeping mission’s legitimacy. | 3B.1, 2B.9, 2B.10 |
| **Germany and Russia spar over a leaked audio on missiles for Ukraine. Berlin promises to investigate** | AP | 4 Mar 2024 | https://apnews.com/article/russia-germany-ukraine-taurus-missiles-recording-de408772f1edf3bd2f98fd5a3f64da3c | Germany treated the intercepted Taurus discussion as a security incident and promised investigation. This shows procedural accountability after a command-and-control failure, not state violence or repression. | 3B.1, 2B.9, 1B.3 |
| **German minister says no political decision made on sending Taurus to Ukraine** | Reuters via ThePrint | 5 Mar 2024 | https://theprint.in/world/german-minister-says-no-political-decision-made-on-sending-taurus-to-ukraine/1989822/ | Pistorius said the intercepted call showed there was no political decision to send Taurus and called the breach an individual mistake. This is relevant as a corrective response, but it does not indicate arbitrary punishment or unlawful violence by the government. | 3B.1, 2B.9, 1B.3 |

## Negative evidence / search gap

- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Scholz ordered or tolerated torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, extrajudicial killing, or arbitrary punishment.
- I also found **no reliable evidence** of a domestic state-violence campaign against residents in Germany in 2024.
- The record is therefore mostly **absence-of-harm evidence plus civilian-protection diplomacy**, not a direct case of preventing domestic repression.

## Synthesis for 3B.1

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz’s 2024 posture was consistent with protecting civilians and limiting unlawful force, especially abroad.
- **Why:** he repeatedly backed ceasefires, humanitarian access, IHL compliance, and investigation after civilian harm.
- **What I did not find:** evidence of state violence, torture, disappearances, political imprisonment, extrajudicial killing, or arbitrary punishment attributable to his government.
- **Overall:** favorable on 3B.1, but the evidence is mostly indirect because Germany was not engaged in a domestic repression context.
